articles/en/dopamine-prediction.title: Dopamine signals prediction
panels: A ping, and my hand moves…
When a notification sounds, it's almost impossible not to check.
Dopamine tracks less pleasure than reward prediction error: the gap between expected and actual.
A clear cue for good habits
Put a clear cue in front of good habits, and clear away the cues for bad ones.
Telling wanting apart from liking keeps you from being pulled along.

articles/en/exercise-hippocampus.title: A year of walking grew the hippocampus
panels: With age, the hippocampus, the brain's memory hub, shrinks a little every year.
In a PNAS study, a year of aerobic walking grew the hippocampus by about 2%.
Walk one stop on the way home. Tie it to the same time each day and it becomes a habit.
Exercise raises BDNF, which supports connections in the hippocampus.

articles/en/habit-66-days.title: Not 21 days, and different for everyone
panels: Despite the "21 days to a habit" claim, it can still feel hard.
Measured time to automaticity ranged from 18 to 254 days, with a median of 66.
Drop the deadline and attach the behavior to a situation: when and where.
Skipping a day didn't matter. The basal ganglia slowly take over the automation.

articles/en/morning-light.title: The power of 10 minutes of morning light
panels: The reason sleep comes late at night often lies in the morning.
Morning light travels through cells in the eye to reset the body clock in the suprachiasmatic nucleus.
Get 10 minutes of light outdoors after waking, and dim the lights in the evening.
At night, the pineal gland releases melatonin on schedule, and sleep arrives.

articles/en/sleep-memory.title: Memories sorted while you sleep
panels: Cutting sleep on a day you learned something can cost you what you studied.
During slow-wave sleep, the hippocampus replays the day and moves it into long-term memory.
Review for 10 minutes before bed, keep a fixed bedtime, and dim bright lights.
After 7 or more hours of sleep, yesterday's learning stays more firmly.

articles/en/ten-percent-myth.title: Only 10% of the brain?
panels: The "10% of the brain" claim beloved by movies and ads has no evidence behind it.
The brain can't afford to leave parts idle; it selects the circuits it needs.
Practice at a slightly harder level, and take care of sleep and exercise.
It changes as you use it
Neuroplasticity: like London taxi drivers' hippocampus, the brain changes with use.
